tweets.text:
Some industry commentary regarding a few claims recently on memory + Softbank Turbine defaulting.

- On claims that LTAs are "meaningless while prices fall": 

$MU: "strategic customer agreements cannot be unilaterally canceled.  Customers are obligated to pay for their committed volumes whether they take delivery or not"

"These are take or pay agreements and there are no contractual outs for our customers from these agreements"

Regarding historical contracts breaking: "These LTAs that we used to have never had any binding terms." The new SCAs contain extensive contractual obligations

Regarding Elon's claims on Softbank defaulting on Turbines:

Question from Morgan Stanley to $GE Vernova CEO on whether they see cancellations or financing difficulties with counterparties on their turbine orders:

“No… we are not”

TLDR:
- Micron states LTAs/SCAs are noncancellable take/pay (where counterparties are hyperscalers). And that these types are different from historical memory cancellations. 

- On Softbank turbine orders, GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said it wasn't seeing customer financing disruptions, requests to exit turbine reservations, or slowdowns. 

Maybe Elon's claims are more narrow, but should be evaluated more closely given competitive interests vs. Softbank/OpenAI.

Don’t hold onto grudges, especially things that are fairly trivial in the grand scheme of things. 

I’ve spent the week at my father’s side as he doesn’t have much time left. 

I should have let some differences go a long time ago. 

At the end, you realize you didn’t particularly care that much, and it was simply pride and ego. 

That falls very quickly when you register that someone you care about will no longer exist.

You do in fact have the choice not to care about things that your ego says you should care about.

Maximize your time with the people you love. Forgive quickly.

Sivers has a tremendous opportunity for CPO/NPO/Pluggables but I’m afraid it’s not being communicated properly. 

It’s understandable here since EETimes is more technical oriented, but I hope this messaging gets communicated better in the next earnings call.

Det er der tilsyneladende ikke råd til, fordi kommunen skal finansiere en myriade af projektansatte, der arbejder med strategier for affaldssortering, integration, normkritisk tænkning og alverdens andre projekter i deres egen lille voksen-SFO.

Man kan ganske enkelt ikke overlade magten til venstrefløjen ret længe ad gangen, uden at det tilsyneladende ender i et administrativt freakshow, hvor bureaukrati, strategier og projektstillinger vokser, mens de borgernære kerneopgaver bliver nedprioriteret.

Det er svært at se det som andet end et grotesk eksempel på en kommune, der har mistet blikket for sine egentlige opgaver.

probably the most underrated AI launch this week - Meta Muse is now powered by their frontier model Wonder Full (which is opus 5.5 grade), big deal for a few reasons:

- muse was already good powered by a less intelligent muse model, now a opus 5.5 level model is slapped on. going to be very hard to compete. 

- this is a real threat to anthropic & openai’s LLM market share. imo agents are the primary way people will interact with AI. if Meta can ship a personal *and competent* superintelligence that does work + leisure then that’s a sticky moat.

- active memory & active focus features means muse will be VERY intuitive, it’ll just know what you want and do it without asking.

- the 1st muse model only came out 7 months ago (!!) that’s a hell of a sprint to frontier level. meta’s shipping velocity has gone vertical.
